answer: The handbook's communication tier list puts pull requests at the top (S tier), then request for comments and GitHub issues (A tier), then public Slack channels (B tier) [1]. At the bottom, email is E tier and tapping someone on the shoulder to ask "You got a minute?" is F tier (the worst) [2]. The list favors public, written, asynchronous channels and ranks interruptive ones lowest, though some entries are jokes [3]. Separately, the customer success page says email is usually one of the worst ways to reach PostHog's ICP (ideal customer profile), which is why CSMs invite customers to Slack [4].

- Use your Brex or Revolut for all work-related expenses, not a personal card [4].
- Expenses over $75 or £75 need itemized receipts and an updated memo within 14 days [5].
- Travel is economy by default [6].
When in doubt, ask your team lead for context, not permission [7].

answer: Sign with either Secretive or 1Password; Secretive is slightly preferred because it keeps the key in the macOS Secure Enclave [1]. With Secretive: create a key named "Git signing key" with Protection Level Notify, then in Secretive > Integrations choose Git Signing and select that key [2]. Paste the ~/.gitconfig and ~/.gitallowedsigners snippets into those files, merging into existing content rather than replacing it [3]. Set SSH_AUTH_SOCK for your shell as Secretive instructs [4]. Then add your public key in GitHub SSH keys settings with key type Signing Key [5]. Test with an empty commit on a new branch and push it; you should see a green Verified badge [6]. With 1Password, follow the 1Password git commit signing guide [7]. Afterwards, enable "Flag unsigned commits as unverified" in your GitHub profile [8].

answer: Usually yes, but not by editing the events. First the customer must stop sending the data, by redacting client-side or setting up a CDP transformation [1]. For customers spending $20K+ a year, the Clickhouse team may be able to write a targeted deletion query, with no guarantees [5].

answer:
Your first three months of commission are paid at 100% fixed OTE, calculated from your start date [1]. Because July 21st is after the 15th, the example for a mid-month start applies: a Jan 17th start gets two months of fixed OTE in the first quarter and one in the next, then two months of quota'ed commission [2]. The handbook's timeline for a 7/21/2025 hire shows the same: Q3 is 1 month not employed plus 2 months at 100% fixed OTE, and Q4 is 1 month at 100% fixed OTE plus 2 months of 'your attainment' OTE [3].

So: August and September (Q3) and October (Q4) are fixed at 100% OTE, and from November your commission is based on your quota attainment.

Check the request against the eligibility criteria, work out the amount, then issue credits or a refund through Billing Admin and Stripe.

- Eligibility: the request must come within 30 days of the billing date [1], and the account must show no signs of fraud or abuse [2]. Repeat cases are handled more strictly: third incidents and beyond may be declined unless circumstances are extraordinary [3].
- Who handles it: for in-app tickets, Support reviews the request, issues the refund or credits and replies to the customer [4]. For large accounts managed by an AE, the AE may lead the conversation and loop in Support or RevOps [5].
- Amount: use the pricing calculator for baseline and overage volumes; the difference is the refund amount [6].
- Credit or refund: issue credits if the period hasn't ended and the invoice isn't finalized [7]. Refunds are initiated through Billing Admin and finalized in Stripe via a credit note [8].
- Escalate to RevOps for big customers (spending $1,667+ monthly) [9], and note that Support should not create or modify invoices [10].

- We have final discretion on who gets the deal [6].

The customer needs an Organization on the EU or US Cloud, and you need billing admin access (ask Raquel or Simon) [1]. Add the trial under Trials > Add Trial, setting the expiration date to whatever is needed, e.g. 2 weeks, or 4 weeks for larger ($100k+) customers [2]. For existing paying customers, ask Mine to update Stripe and billing admin so revenue numbers are unaffected and the customer isn't billed during the trial [3]. Before the trial ends, create a new subscription and update Billing Admin so the transition back to a paid plan is smooth [7]. The excerpts don't describe how to restrict the trial to one specific product beyond the form's Target field (paid, teams, enterprise).

answer: Extensions aren't the norm, but you can ask. The 12-month window is meant to be firm, though exceptions are possible [1]. You need to explain clearly why you couldn't use the credit in time and show evidence of recent progress or changes; the Customer Success team reviews requests manually [2]. That happens automatically on a standard paid plan, with an email letting them know and a one-time $500 credit bonus to soften the transition [5].
